content.title: About
content.content: White onion is a vegetable obtained from the bulb of Allium cepa. It has a characteristic sharp taste and aroma, and its thin white skin peels easily. Onions are eaten raw and are also used in cooking for soups, sauces, salads, and countless dishes.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Onion belongs to the Amaryllidaceae family and is one of the oldest cultivated plants, grown by humans for over 5,000 years.
White onions contain sulfur compounds that release volatile gases when cut, causing eyes to water.
The vegetable has different names worldwide: in the UK it is called "white onion", in France "oignon blanc".
A bulb consists of several layers, each being a modified leaf.
Onion is often used in folk medicine as a remedy for colds and to aid digestion.

items.title: Rich in antioxidants
items.content: Onions contain quercetin and sulfides that help protect cells from oxidative stress.

items.title: Supports cardiovascular health
items.content: Sulfur compounds can help lower cholesterol levels and improve vessel function.

items.title: Contains vitamin C
items.content: Vitamin C boosts immunity and participates in collagen synthesis.

items.title: Source of prebiotics
items.content: Fructans in onions promote the growth of beneficial gut bacteria.

items.title: Low‑calorie food
items.content: Onion provides few calories while delivering satiety thanks to its fiber content.

items.title: Allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to onion, ranging from skin rashes to respiratory issues.

items.title: Stomach irritation
items.content: People with sensitive stomachs may experience heartburn or discomfort after eating raw onion.

items.title: Medication interactions
items.content: Sulfur compounds can enhance the effects of anticoagulants, so moderation is advised for those on blood‑thinners.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Onion can be eaten raw in salads, sandwiches, and pickles. It is often finely diced for sauces, guacamole, or added to fresh vegetable mixes. For a milder flavor, onion can be marinated in vinegar or lemon juice.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store onions in a cool, dry, well‑ventilated place, preferably in a mesh bag. For longer storage, keep them in the refrigerator’s vegetable drawer, but avoid moisture to prevent spoilage.
